This small plot near the house I keep for our yam and cassava with some vegetables between. I am too old now to buy fertilizer for such a small piece — I just spread the household ash and goat droppings I collect through the year, which has always been enough for root crops here. The seed I save myself from last harvest, as my mother taught me, and I do not spray chemicals on food we eat ourselves. My grandson helps me with the heavy mound-making, but most of the weeding I still do with my own hands.
